patches.value: Use one ambient Euclidean representation throughout: Space d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) = PiLp 2 (fun _ => ℝ). Its norm and real inner product are the Euclidean ones; PiLp.inner_apply identifies the latter with the coordinate dot product. Fin n labels the original n coordinates by j.val + 1; it introduces neither a missing endpoint nor an extra coordinate. PiLp.single 2 j 1 is the unit vector in coordinate j, so spatial is the Fréchet derivative evaluated on that vector. ut and utt are successive ordinary time derivatives, uxx successive same-coordinate spatial derivatives, and utx is the spatial derivative of ut. Under H002 equality of mixed derivatives identifies utx with the time derivative of ux; proving this identification is part of T004/T007, not a hidden assumption. densityTime is the ACTUAL time derivative of the density, not an assumed product formula. The parameter u is an arbitrary total ambient representative; H002 and all geometric hypotheses concern only positive times. Any source map extends by zero for t≤0, without requiring boundary regularity, and restriction recovers it. Since positive times form an open set, derivatives of all orders and energy germs there depend only on that restriction. No conclusion concerns the chosen exterior values. ContDiffOn uses (∞ : ℕ∞ω), meaning every finite derivative order, not ω (analyticity) or the top element of ℕ∞ω. Header definitions assert no regularity or integrability. The total Bochner integral in energy gains its intended finite Lebesgue meaning only after T003 proves integrability. volume is standard normalized Euclidean Lebesgue measure; EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp identifies it with product coordinate Lebesgue measure. In N002, iteratedFDeriv of positive natural order is the multilinear encoding of all mixed space/time derivatives: evaluation on coordinate unit vectors recovers them, and multilinearity plus the coordinate basis gives the converse. All this is in the same Euclidean representation; local product-coordinate measure transport in T008 is checked inside that obligation. No M ports are retained: the four supplied library theorems are used directly under their actual hypotheses. H003 is preserved although the source proof never needs the norm of q. For measures, ENNReal.ofReal ((2*R)^n) encodes a nonnegative real box volume; R>0 and the explicit non-top clause prevent treating an infinite mass as a real finite integral. Integrable means almost everywhere strong measurability together with finite integral of the norm. The supplied dominated-convergence theorem requires these norm and measurability conditions, not merely pointwise convergence. For the scalar FTC, ℝ supplies completeness; the derivative must exist on the unordered closed interval and its function must be interval integrable. Fubini will be used with finite restricted coordinate measures, hence s-finite, and a genuinely integrable real function. These typeclass capabilities are properties of the chosen standard spaces and measures, not additional hypotheses on the wave map.
